name: @agentic-toolkit/adh-ecosystem-panes
description: An ecosystem's own sub-resources as panes: Applications, Storage Buckets, Users and Messaging — the four surfaces of an ecosystem that are typed against adh's backend API.
comment:tier: VOCABULARY, not mechanism — see scripts/check_boundaries.py. These panes are typed against `@agentic-toolkit/adh-api-types` (adh's generated OpenAPI request/response bodies), which the guard bans from any `@agentic-toolkit/<x>` package whose <x> is not adh/adh-*. That import is the whole reason this is a package of its own rather than four more files in `ecosystem-config`: that package IS mechanism (an org site and a product host both mount it against their own backends), and widening it to name adh's API types would have made it unportable in a way nothing else there is. The `adh-` prefix is what puts this package on the right side of that line, and the directory is `features/` only because the tsup/vitest presets live there.
comment:exports: see @agentic-toolkit/adh for the full rationale. The barrel is entirely `use client` panes, and tsup hoists that directive over the whole chunk — so the two things here that are not panes get their own directive-free entries (the same split the tsup preset describes for ./parse and ./tables). ./bucket-types is the bucket type catalogue; its non-UI consumers are the reason: tools/check-bucket-types-drift.py reads the source text to diff it against the backend schema, and the hub's bucket-types Playwright spec derives its expected count by CALLING buildAvailableTypes() in node — through the barrel that import would drag every pane, react-query and next/navigation into a bare node context. ./parse is the Storage group's URL grammar, and its consumer is a host's ROUTE: the hub's storage page is a Server Component that has to parse (and 404) before it renders anything. That Playwright spec is also the only consumer in the fleet that arrives through `require` — the hub package declares no `type`, so Playwright compiles the spec to CJS — which is why ./bucket-types carries a `default` beside its `import` and ./parse does not: conditions are matched in order, so `default` is reached ONLY by a resolver that matched nothing above it, and a subpath offering neither `require` nor `default` fails that resolver with ERR_PACKAGE_PATH_NOT_EXPORTED — Node's wording for `no condition matched` is the same as for a subpath that is genuinely absent, which makes it read as a missing key that is visibly right there.
